text:
It is truly heartwarming to observe how cinema has so brilliantly prepared us for the rigors of adolescence, teaching us that the complex socio-political landscape of high school is best navigated not through dialogue or empathy, but through sudden, unprovoked bursts of synchronized movement. We are led to believe that the crushing weight of academic pressure and social anxiety can be effectively resolved by simply breaking into a perfectly timed routine, because nothing says "conflict resolution" like a well-rehearsed hip-hop sequence.

In this utopian vision, the primary material of a candle is not wax, but rather the sheer, unadulterated hope that a dramatic spotlight will save us from having to actually talk to our parents.
